item.title: ASANTE-MUHAMMAD/PARKER: The Truth About Trump Accounts and Black Wealth
item.description: Trump Accounts, while seemingly beneficial, are likely to widen the racial wealth gap due to their opt-in structure and reliance on contributions from families and employers, making them a form of "fool's gold" for Black families, while Baby Bonds offer a more progressive approach to wealth-building for low-income families. The post ASANTE-MUHAMMAD/PARKER: The Truth About Trump Accounts and Black Wealth appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: President Donald Trump Says Kennedy Center to Close for Two Years
item.description: President Donald Trump has announced the temporary closure of the Kennedy Center for two years on July 4th for construction and revitalization, following low ticket sales and pushback from artists and audiences alike. The post President Donald Trump Says Kennedy Center to Close for Two Years appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Afeni Evans: A Full-Fledged Abolitionist Tells Her Story
item.description: Afeni Evans, a D.C.-based organizer and former member of the U.S. Army, has become an abolitionist and community organizer, using her experiences to fuel her fight against the military industrial complex and state-sanctioned violence. The post Afeni Evans: A Full-Fledged Abolitionist Tells Her Story appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Kendrick Lamar Makes Hip Hop History at 2026 Grammy Awards
item.description: Kendrick Lamar made hip-hop history at the 68th Grammy Awards, becoming the hip-hop artist with the most Grammy awards, and emphasizing the importance of hip-hop on overall culture. item.description: The Washington Wizards celebrated John Wall's legacy with a victory over the Milwaukee Bucks, a court renovation in his name, a donation to his foundation, and a Captain of the Day appearance at Howard University. item.title: Grammy History, Cultural Impact, and the Return of Michael Jackson
item.description: Lionsgate has released a new trailer for "Michael," a biopic charting Michael Jackson's rise to fame from his earliest days with the Jackson 5 to his emergence as a global phenomenon, set to release on April 24. The post Grammy History, Cultural Impact, and the Return of Michael Jackson appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Mezzo-Soprano Denyce Graves Uncovers New Joy in Retirement
item.description: Denyce Graves, a multi-Grammy-winning mezzo-soprano, retired from the Metropolitan Opera after 31 years, and is now leading The Denyce Graves Foundation and directing the opera "Treemonisha" at the Washington National Opera. The post Mezzo-Soprano Denyce Graves Uncovers New Joy in Retirement appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Maryland Reports $1 Billion Decline in Net Position as Economic Headwinds Grow
item.description: Maryland's Annual Comprehensive Financial Report for fiscal year 2025 shows slower economic growth, mounting losses in the federal workforce, and increasing strain on state finances, with a projected $2.95 billion shortfall for fiscal year 2026. The post Maryland Reports $1 Billion Decline in Net Position as Economic Headwinds Grow appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: We Have Come This Far By Faith
item.description: Black History Month is a time to reflect on the progress made and to take action to protect the gains made, as faith has always been a source of strength in the face of adversity. The post We Have Come This Far By Faith appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Legal Challenge Filed Over Sweeping Suspension of Immigrant Visas
item.description: A coalition of U.S. citizens, immigrant families, and nonprofit organizations has filed a federal lawsuit to challenge the Trump administration's suspension of immigrant visa processing for people from 75 countries, arguing that the policy is discriminatory and violates federal immigration law. The post Legal Challenge Filed Over Sweeping Suspension of Immigrant Visas appeared first on The Washington Informer.
